stories.headline: S&P 500 EXTENDS CPI SELLOFF TO A SECOND DAY, DOWN 0.58% AS NASDAQ LEADS LOSSES
stories.body: Equities continued their post-CPI retreat Wednesday, with the S&P 500 closing at 7,349 (-0.58%) and the Nasdaq falling to 25,912 (-0.76%). The 10-year Treasury yield edged up 2 bps to 4.48%, extending a two-day surge of 8 bps since the hot April CPI print. Gold broke higher, gaining +1.2% to $4,733, as investors rotated from risk assets into inflation hedges.

stories.headline: TRUMP ARRIVES IN BEIJING — XI SUMMIT NOW UNDERWAY WITH TARIFF TRUCE EXTENSION ON TABLE
stories.body: President Trump arrived in Beijing for a two-day summit with President Xi Jinping, the first direct meeting since the October 2025 tariff truce. The truce cut China's effective U.S. tariff rate from 41% to 31%; an extension is widely expected alongside Chinese commitments to purchase American soybeans, beef, and Boeing aircraft. Polymarket prices a US-China comprehensive deal at ~50-50 odds by May 31, keeping trade uncertainty embedded in the inflation outlook.

stories.headline: GOLD SURGES TO $4,733, REVERSING YESTERDAY'S LOSS AS DOLLAR WEAKENS ON SUMMIT OPTIMISM
stories.body: Gold gained +1.2% to $4,733, erasing Tuesday's -0.45% decline, as the dollar index (DXY) fell 0.56% to 98.45 — partly driven by trade-deal optimism from the Trump-Xi meeting dampening safe-haven dollar demand. WTI crude slipped 0.66% to $101.20 but remains in its post-Hormuz elevated range; Brent held near $107. The gold rally signals markets are hedging both inflationary persistence and geopolitical tail risk simultaneously.

stories.headline: FED HIKE PROBABILITY HOLDS AT 25-30% AS BOND MARKET PRICES 'HIGHER FOR LONGER' THROUGH 2027
stories.body: CME FedWatch maintains a ~25% probability of at least one Fed rate hike by December 2026, with virtually no chance of a cut priced through end of 2027. The 10-year yield at 4.48% and 30-year at 5.02% are already doing tightening work before any Fed action. Real average hourly wages are down 0.3% year-over-year — workers absorbing the oil shock for now — but the critical watchpoint remains 5Y5Y forward inflation expectations, currently near 2.4%.

stories.headline: 76-TEAM MARCH MADNESS ERA BEGINS NEXT SEASON — POWER CONFERENCES TO ABSORB MOST NEW BIDS
stories.body: With the NCAA's May 7 vote to expand March Madness from 68 to 76 teams official, attention shifts to how the eight new at-large spots will be distributed. Power conferences (ACC, Big Ten, Big 12, SEC) are projected to capture the bulk of the additional bids given their strength metrics, while mid-major leagues gain modest benefit. The expansion is funded by ~$300 million in beer, wine, and spirits sponsorship deals, marking the NCAA's first alcohol advertising partnerships.

stories.headline: PISTONS-CAVS GAME 5 TIPS TONIGHT (8 PM ET) WITH SERIES EVEN AT 2-2
stories.body: Detroit hosts Cleveland tonight at Little Caesars Arena in a pivotal Game 5, with the Eastern Conference Semifinals tied 2-2 after Donovan Mitchell's historic 43-point (39 in the second half) Game 4 performance pulled the Cavs level. The Knicks await the winner in the ECF after sweeping Philadelphia 4-0, including an NBA playoff-record-tying 25 3-pointers in Game 4. San Antonio holds a 3-2 series lead over Minnesota in the West.

stories.headline: NFL 2026 SCHEDULES RELEASE TOMORROW — DEFENDING CHAMP SEAHAWKS GET PRIMETIME WEEK 1 KICKOFF
stories.body: All 32 NFL team schedules drop Thursday at 5 PM PT; the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks are confirmed to host the Week 1 NBC Kickoff game at Lumen Field. Teams continue maneuvering ahead of the June 1 salary cap deadline — when dead-cap penalty cuts are halved — with WR AJ Brown trade speculation and QB contract situations around Baker Mayfield and CJ Stroud among the largest unresolved offseason storylines.

stories.headline: NIL ARMS RACE RESHAPES COLLEGE FOOTBALL LANDSCAPE AS PROGRAMS REVEAL SPENDING TOTALS
stories.body: With the January transfer portal window closed and spring ball complete, programs are disclosing NIL rev-share commitments that reveal a widening financial gap: LSU committed $25-30 million for roster building on top of Lane Kiffin's $13M salary, while BYU pledged $10M-plus extra to retain Kalani Sitake. Oklahoma State imported the most FBS transfers (50) under new head coach Eric Morris. The compressed portal window — now January-only after the spring window was permanently eliminated — concentrated bidding and drove prices sharply higher.

deepDive.title: Fed Funds Futures: How a '25% Rate Hike Probability' Is Actually Calculated
content: Today's brief references a 25% probability of a Fed rate hike by December 2026. That number is everywhere in financial media, but its origin is rarely explained. It comes from the CME FedWatch tool, which reads implied rate probabilities from 30-day Fed funds futures contracts. These contracts trade on the CME as prices equal to 100 minus the expected average effective federal funds rate for their delivery month. When the CME says there's a 25% chance of a hike, it's extracting that signal from where traders are pricing December futures — not from a survey or a model, but from real money at risk.

The mechanics work as follows. Suppose the current Fed funds target is 4.50–4.75% (effective rate ~4.625%) and December futures trade at 95.375, implying a 4.625% expected rate. If the only two outcomes are 'hold at 4.625%' or 'hike to 4.875%' (one 25-basis-point move), then the implied probability of a hike equals: (expected rate − hold rate) / (hike rate − hold rate) = (4.625 − 4.625) / (4.875 − 4.625) = 0%. But if the futures imply 4.6875% — exactly halfway — that's a 25% hike probability: (4.6875 − 4.625) / 0.25 = 25%. The logic is simply probability-weighted averaging across possible outcomes.

The critical limitation is that futures markets are not forecasts — they are risk-adjusted expectations. Traders demand compensation for uncertainty, so the implied probability embeds a risk premium. In 2022, Fed funds futures systematically underpriced the actual pace of hikes as the market anchored too heavily on the prior low-rate regime. Historically, when the CME shows a 25% hike probability, the Fed actually ends up hiking roughly 30-40% of the time — the market discounts tail risk. The tool is best read as a real-time consensus on the balance of risks, not a prediction of what the Fed will do.

Why does this matter today? Even a 25% hike probability — well short of a base case — has already materially tightened financial conditions. When hike odds rose from 21.5% Monday to 25% post-CPI, the 10-year yield jumped 6 basis points and equity valuations compressed through higher discount rates. This is the Fed's 'shadow channel': it doesn't have to actually hike for financial conditions to tighten — the market does the work preemptively. The Trump-Xi summit creates a potential release valve: a credible tariff reduction would cut the inflationary impulse, pull hike probabilities back toward zero, and allow a meaningful equity relief rally. That's why today's summit news is simultaneously a macro and market story.
